**Context resolved**

- **All three incidents confirmed** via their recovery commits, each landing the
  payload in git under `eval_results/issue_2162/`:
  `9fddd9e1a6` (P5 pilot gate report, 25 lines),
  `6eec51c77e` (P8 stage-2 phase sentinel, 21 lines),
  `92f25415ee` (margin leg: `margin_leg_sentinel.json` 74 lines +
  `upload_done.json` 69 lines). Nothing is currently missing, as the body states.
- **Nearest prior art is #1449** (`daily-fix: plan-glob vs uploader
  allow-pattern parity check`, completed) — landed as a rule in
  `.claude/rules/upload-policy.md` plus the `code-reviewer.md` Step 0.65
  parity sub-check. It is COMPLEMENTARY, not duplicative, and its own text
  is what proves the gap: it binds the union of upload filters to "every
  artifact class **the plan declares as persisted**". All three #2162 losses
  were files the plan never declared (a pilot gate report, a phase sentinel,
  an upload-completion marker), so a declaration-bounded parity check
  provably cannot reach them. #2187 is the inverse, residue direction:
  files that EXIST on disk and match NO upload glob.
- **Second, sharper mechanical finding (new, not in the body).** The
  `upload-verifier`'s own Step 1 enumeration structurally cannot see this
  class either, for two independent reasons: (a) both `find` roots are the
  repo checkout (`/workspace/explore-persona-space`), while a per-issue
  out-root is typically `/workspace/issue<N>_out/` — outside it; and (b) the
  broad by-issue-number sweep additionally filters `-size +10k`, while the
  three lost files were 740 B, 754 B and 2,580 B. So this is not only an
  agent-diligence gap, as the body frames it — the specified enumeration
  recipe misses the class twice over. Both holes are in scope for the plan.
- **Reuse discovery (complete, untruncated).** `scripts/verify_uploads.py`
  (1,636 lines) is the shared mechanical verifier the agent runs; its
  `run_verification()` assembles named `report["checks"][...]` rows, which is
  the natural plug-in point for a mechanical residue check. No existing
  out-root sweep helper exists anywhere in `scripts/` or `src/` — the
  `issue<N>_*` upload/verify scripts are all per-issue. Nothing to reuse;
  nothing to duplicate.
- **Existing verifier coverage read.** Step 2.9 already does a per-file
  NAME-SET reconciliation (`comm` diff of `find` vs `git ls-tree`) — but for
  GIT destinations only (#537). The HF/out-root side has no equivalent, which
  is the shape to mirror rather than invent.
- **Recursion guard.** The body carried no `## Provenance`
  `workflow_fix_target:` line, so `is_workflow_fix_session(2187)` was False —
  a workflow-fix task that could have auto-filed more workflow-fix tasks, and
  whose Step 2 minimum plan-review floor was unarmed. Added the `wf-fix` tag
  and a `## Provenance` section naming `.claude/rules/pods.md` as the primary
  target; the guard now reads True. The `## Goal` was not touched.

### BLOCKER — independently confirmed by the orchestrator before acting

Plan v1 §4.2(A) step 2 built the permanent-home set from **unscoped** whole-repo
basenames (`git` tree listing for `origin/issue-<N>` **and** `HEAD`). Replaying
v1's own §6 item 2 FAIL-direction test against the live tree (178,914 tracked
files at HEAD) — orchestrator-verified, not taken on the critic's word:

| Motivating loss | Basename hits at HEAD | Colliding owners |
|---|---|---|
| `pilot_gate_report.json` | **8** | `eval_results/issue_{1417 x2, 1739 x3, 1774, 2094 x2}/` |
| `upload_done.json` | **4** | `eval_results/issue_1768/{model_text_2x2, on_target, on_target_r4, on_target_r5}/` |
| `stage2_results.json` | 0 | — |

So for a no-permanent-home issue, residue = {`stage2_results.json`} only:
**2 of the 3 motivating losses false-PASS today.** Both colliding names are
CONVENTIONAL — `pilot_gate_report.json` is the built-in #2054 pilot-gate output
name, `upload_done.json` a recurring completion-marker name — so incident
classes 1 and 3 would have been structurally invisible to the new check BY
DESIGN, permanently. v1's §6 item 2 acceptance criterion ("FAIL naming all
three files") was false as written, and §8's "basename collision — Low
likelihood" was wrong by an order of magnitude for the whole-tree form.

Root cause of the miss: v1's §12 assumption-1 predicate trace covered only the
pre-recovery INCIDENT-TIME tree, never the tree the check actually runs against.
This is the exact failure mode #2187 exists to prevent, reproduced one level up
in the fix's own verification design — caught pre-implementation, which is the
point of the floor.

**Fix carried into v2:** scope both git-tree listings to issue-owned paths
(issue token as a path component) BEFORE taking basenames. Verified to preserve
the PASS direction — all four recovered #2162 files sit under
`eval_results/issue_2162/` on `origin/issue-2162`. The HF arm is unchanged
(caller-supplied prefixes are issue-scoped by construction). The regression pin
is the assertion that FAIL names ALL THREE basenames against the live repo: it
fails under v1's design and passes under the scoped one.

### MINOR folded into v2

1. **v1 K1 carried a factual error** — it claimed the watcher reconcile passes
   use `stop`, not `terminate`. `terminate_pod()` is in fact called directly,
   bypassing `cmd_terminate` and both guards, from `backend_poll.py` (4 sites:
   workload-crash cleanup + the #770/#1667 no-port wedge arm) and
   `pod_audit.py:648` (`audit-stale --terminate-stale`). Consequence is an
   accuracy + scope-of-claim fix, not a design change: those paths cannot be
   false-refused by the new token (they never enter the guard) and are
   crash/stale-cleanup, outside the demonstrated verify-then-terminate class.
   v2 corrects K1, scopes the "mechanically forces every terminate path" claim
   to the `pod.py terminate` chokepoint, and widens assumption 3's grep to
   enumerate direct `terminate_pod(` call sites.
2. **Undecided interaction made a decision** — PASS-note-without-token PLUS
   `--skip-upload-verify` was left unspecified by v1 (`skip_flag` is consulted
   only when no PASS exists). v2 picks one behavior, states why, and pins that
   exact combo in the guard-test list.
3. Assumption 3's verify-at-implementation posture judged adequate as-is
   (loud refusal carrying its own remediation recipe; K1 pre-registers the WARN
   downgrade) — no change beyond the grep widening.

### What the revise round bought

v1 would have shipped a durability check **structurally blind to 2 of the 3
losses it was built to catch.** Its permanent-home set took basenames from the
UNSCOPED whole repo tree, so conventional filenames resolved cross-issue:
measured at HEAD, `pilot_gate_report.json` at 8 paths under other issues and
`upload_done.json` at 4 — both conventional names (the built-in #2054
pilot-gate output; a recurring completion-marker name), so incident classes 1
and 3 would have been invisible permanently, by design.

Root cause of the near-miss: v1's predicate trace covered only the
pre-recovery INCIDENT-TIME tree, never the tree the check actually runs
against — the same class of verification gap #2187 exists to close,
reproduced one level up in the fix's own acceptance criteria.

v2 scopes both git-tree listings to issue-owned paths (issue token as a path
component, digit-boundary guarded) BEFORE taking basenames. Orchestrator-measured
both directions before persisting:

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| Filter on `origin/issue-2162` (PASS direction) | keeps all four recovered files |
| Filter for issue 999999 (FAIL direction) | 0 matches |
| Digit boundary (`issue_21620` vs 2162) | 0 spurious hits |
| `terminate_pod(` sites (the K1 correction) | `backend_poll.py` 4 real calls, `pod_audit.py` 1, `pod_lifecycle.py` 1 post-guard |

Two accuracy fixes also landed: v1's K1 wrongly claimed the watcher/poller
paths use `stop` rather than `terminate` (five sites call `terminate_pod()`
directly, bypassing both guards), so the "mechanically forces every
experiment-pod terminate" claim is now scoped to the `pod.py terminate`
chokepoint with the bypass set disclosed; and the previously-undecided
PASS-without-token x `--skip-upload-verify` interaction is now a stated
decision (skip waives the token with a LOUD WARN — a PASS-without-token pod
must not be blocked harder than a no-marker pod under the same flag) pinned by
a named guard test.

### Carried into implementation

- **Regression pin:** the live-tree `--issue 999999` assertion that FAIL names
  ALL THREE basenames is **false under v1's design and true under v2's** — it
  discriminates the exact defect rather than restating it.
- **Disclosed residuals (not mitigated, deliberately):** within-issue basename
  collisions can still mask residue (#2162 itself carries two committed
  `pilot_gate_report.json` under different subdirs); the five direct
  `terminate_pod()` reaps sit outside both enforcement layers by design —
  adding a marker precondition there would block the billing-leak teardowns

- **Implementer notes from round 2:** confirm `plan.md` resolves to `v2.md`
